# Sorting the branches I had already started

::: {.entry-summary-strip}
`2 LASTING MERGES`{.entry-status .status-merged} `2 EXPERIMENTS CLOSED`{.entry-status .status-closed} `PUBLIC PLAN OPENED`{.entry-status}
:::

## Outcome

I did not enter Community Bonding with an empty task list. Several of my Animint2 pull requests were already under review, so I used these three weeks to decide what I should finish first, what needed a redesign, and what was no longer worth pursuing.

The ChIP-seq gallery work and download-size feature merged during this period. I also opened Issue #327 to keep my GSoC updates public and began investigating the GitHub Pages race that became my first coding-period fix.

## Context

Before GSoC, I had already worked on selectors, renderer tests, text rendering, facets, layout, and the gallery. The point of this entry is not to retell March and April; it records the decisions and outcomes from May 1–24.

## What I Did

### May 1–9 — Visible results and useful closure

- Merged [gallery PR #51](https://github.com/animint/gallery/pull/51), which ported the ChIP-seq Large Margin visualization to the current Animint2 gallery.
- Merged [PR #272](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/272), adding file count, row count, total size, and mean size to download-status output.
- [PR #310](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/310) closed without merge after review. The public record gives no final closure reason, so I do not assign one here.

### May 10–16 — Scope and compatibility review

- Re-evaluated [PR #291](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/291), the broad `RJSONIO` to `jsonlite` migration.
- Reviewed compatibility risks across scalars, vectors, data frames, `NULL`, nested lists, and automatic unboxing.
- Rechecked open multiline, facet, selector, renderer, and CI branches instead of treating all of them as equally ready.

### May 17–24 — Public plan and CI race

- Opened [Issue #327](https://github.com/animint/animint2/issues/327) as my public GSoC plan and update log.
- Closed/reprioritized PR #291 after the maintainer asked us to focus on more important issues. The compatibility tests remained useful research.
- Opened [Issue #324](https://github.com/animint/animint2/issues/324) after tracing `R_coverage` and `JS_coverage` to the same mutable GitHub Pages test repository.
- Opened [PR #330](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/330) with a test-first guard and job-specific repository names derived from `TEST_SUITE`.
- Organized the active backlog into likely-to-merge, review-heavy, collaborative, exploratory, pre-midterm, and post-midterm workstreams.

## Learnings

PR #291 and PR #310 did not merge, but they still left useful evidence about compatibility and browser-test design. The CI investigation also gave me a more specific explanation than “flaky”: two jobs were changing the same external repository at the same time.

## Challenges / Notes

The difficult part was deciding what not to carry into the coding period. Existing work did not automatically deserve more implementation time simply because I had already started it.

## Next Week Targets

Merge the isolated-repository CI fix, finish the PR #292 review, and continue the focused revisions on PR #288 and PR #285.
